samples.summary: Component docstring is now stale: it still states "Each row links to that document's detailed analytics (`/w/:workspaceId/analytics/:id`)", which is exactly the behavior this change removes for non-manageable rows. The new inline comment at line 89 contradicts the header comment.
samples.evidence: Line 25-26: "Each row links to that document's detailed analytics" vs. line 92 `{r.canManage && (<Link ...>)}`.

samples.summary: Layering smell: `canManage` is a caller-scoped authorization predicate but was added to the warehouse-owned `DocumentBreakdown` type, forcing the StarRocks layer to fabricate a meaningless `canManage: false` placeholder (same pattern already tolerated for `title: ''`). A controller-level enriched type (e.g. `DocumentBreakdown & { title: string; canManage: boolean }`) would keep the warehouse row type honest and remove the dummy value that a future caller could read as "not a manager".
samples.evidence: documentRows() returns `{ documentId, title: '', views, uniqueVisitors, canManage: false }` — the warehouse has no knowledge of the caller.

samples.summary: Non-manageable rows now render a completely empty action cell with no affordance or explanation; the issue's outcome ("other rows show nothing in that cell") is met, but a muted "—" or tooltip would explain the asymmetry to a member who sees links on some rows only. Purely a taste point, not a spec gap.
